title: Food & Beverage Manufacturing
summary: Co-packing, private label, and specialty ingredient manufacturing characterized by high volume, stringent quality controls, and supply chain complexity.
businessModel: Manufacturing food and beverage products either under proprietary brands, private labels for grocery retailers, or as a contract manufacturer (co-packer) for large CPG companies.
revenueModel: Volume-based unit sales driven by retail distribution expansion or long-term take-or-pay manufacturing contracts with brands.
costStructure: Raw materials/ingredients, packaging, direct labor (line workers), facility overhead (cold storage, utilities), and logistics/freight.
keyKpis: Order Fill Rate (OTIF - On Time In Full)
whyPeLikesIt: Highly defensive, recession-resistant demand profile, stable cash flows, and immense opportunities to drive margin through supply chain optimization and manufacturing lean principles.
investmentThesis: Acquire a niche manufacturer with strong retailer or brand relationships, optimize plant operations to unlock capacity and improve yield, and execute M&A to expand product categories or geographic distribution footprint.
diligenceQuestions: How exposed are the margins to commodity price fluctuations, and what hedging mechanisms are in place?
What is the customer concentration, and are contracts easily cancelable?
Are the facilities SQF (Safe Quality Food) or BRC certified, and what is the recent audit history?
operationalIssues: High material waste/scrap due to poor line changeovers or recipe control.
Inability to pass commodity inflation through to retail customers.
Excessive downtime leading to poor OEE and missed customer orders (OTIF).
aiOpportunities: Machine vision for automated quality inspection on the line.
Predictive demand forecasting to optimize raw material purchasing.
AI-optimized production scheduling to minimize allergen washdowns and changeover time.
risks: Food safety recalls or contamination events (existential threat).
Customer concentration with demanding big-box retailers (e.g., Walmart).
Labor shortages for frontline manufacturing roles.
hundredDayPlan: Conduct a deep dive SKU-level profitability analysis to cull margin-dilutive products.
Implement daily shift-level reporting on Yield, Scrap, and OEE.
Review and tighten quality assurance and food safety protocols.
exitReadiness: A clean, highly automated facility with top-tier SQF audit scores.
Diversified customer base with index-based pricing contracts.
Proven track record of launching and scaling new product innovations.

articleSections.title: Yield Optimization and Scrap Reduction
body: In Food & Beverage (F&B) manufacturing, raw materials and packaging costs routinely account for an overwhelming 60-70% of total operating expenses. Consequently, the most direct, high-impact path to EBITDA expansion is 'Yield Optimization.' If a recipe mathematically requires 100 pounds of raw ingredients, but poor machinery calibration, improper handling, or spillage results in only 92 pounds of saleable, packaged product, that 8% variance instantly destroys the gross margin. We initiate value creation by implementing rigorous, shift-by-shift tracking of material variance and scrap at the individual line level.

We counter this margin leakage by instituting highly standardized operating procedures for ingredient handling and aggressively investing in precision dosing, weighing, and filling equipment. Often, manufacturers intentionally overfill packages—a practice known as 'giveaway'—to ensure regulatory compliance and avoid under-weight penalties. By upgrading to high-speed, highly accurate check-weighers and statistical process control software, we can reduce this giveaway from 4% down to 1%, keeping the product perfectly within legal tolerances while dramatically reducing raw material waste.

The financial leverage of yield optimization is extraordinary. A seemingly modest 2-3% improvement in overall material yield across a high-volume, $150M revenue facility generates massive, pure-profit flow-through to the bottom line without requiring the sales team to acquire a single new customer or raise prices. We expect the Operating Partner to utilize daily 'Scrap Dashboards' to relentlessly hold plant managers accountable for material efficiency, transforming the shop floor culture from volume-obsessed to margin-obsessed.
articleSections.callout: In high-volume F&B manufacturing, the battle for gross margin is won or lost on the plant floor. Yield optimization is the most critical and controllable operational lever.

articleSections.title: Pricing Power and Commodity Hedging
body: F&B manufacturers are dangerously exposed to the volatility of global commodity cycles—fluctuations in the prices of wheat, dairy, edible oils, and corrugated packaging can evaporate margins overnight. Target companies often suffer severe margin compression because they agree to fixed-price, multi-year contracts with powerful, demanding big-box retailers, but are forced to buy their raw ingredients on the unpredictable spot market. The Private Equity playbook requires fundamentally restructuring this asymmetrical pricing model.

We aggressively implement 'Index-Based Pricing' or 'Pass-Through' mechanisms in all new customer contracts. This ensures that any significant raw material inflation is automatically passed down to the buyer, insulating the manufacturer's EBITDA from macro commodity shocks. In scenarios where retailers fiercely resist pass-through pricing, we establish sophisticated, centralized forward-purchasing and hedging strategies. By utilizing financial derivatives or locking in long-term supply contracts when commodity prices dip, we create a predictable, protected margin profile.

Disciplined pricing ensures that the platform actually captures the financial value of its operational improvements, rather than inadvertently subsidizing the retailer's margin through lower prices. For a $200M co-packer, failing to pass through a 10% spike in flour and sugar costs can wipe out $12M in EBITDA. We institute rigorous 'Margin Review Committees' that analyze input costs weekly, ensuring the sales team has the data and mandate to execute immediate, surgical price increases when inflation hits.

articleSections.title: OEE and Maximizing Asset Capacity
body: Building a brand-new, food-grade manufacturing facility is a massively capital-intensive process that can take years to permit and construct. Therefore, unlocking 'hidden capacity' within the existing four walls of the plant is the operational holy grail. We focus relentlessly on maximizing Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE). High downtime in F&B is frequently caused by highly inefficient line changeovers—specifically, the excessive time required to sanitize and wash down production lines when switching between different products, especially to manage severe allergen risks.

We attack this downtime by deploying sophisticated algorithmic scheduling to sequence production runs intelligently. For example, running light-colored products to dark-colored products, or allergen-free runs prior to allergen-containing runs, to legally minimize the frequency of deep washdowns. We then apply 'SMED' (Single-Minute Exchange of Die) Lean principles to the packaging lines, training dedicated changeover 'pit crews' to reduce setup times from hours to mere minutes. This ensures the line is running saleable product as much as humanly possible.

Increasing a facility's OEE from a typical baseline of 60% to a world-class 75% effectively adds an entire 'free' production line to the plant. This allows the business to rapidly scale revenue and onboard new, high-volume customers with absolutely zero CapEx. Furthermore, high OEE ensures perfect 'On-Time In-Full' (OTIF) delivery metrics, which prevents crippling fines from major retailers like Walmart and solidifies the manufacturer's status as a top-tier, reliable supply chain partner.

articleSections.title: SKU Rationalization and Complexity Reduction
body: Over years of operation, F&B manufacturers often wildly proliferate their product offerings in an attempt to appease every minor customer request. This results in a 'long tail' of low-volume, highly complex SKUs that quietly bleed the company's profitability. Complexity is the mortal enemy of manufacturing efficiency; short, bespoke production runs destroy OEE, mandate constant changeovers, and require massive amounts of working capital to be tied up in niche, slow-moving packaging and raw ingredients. We execute a ruthless SKU rationalization program during the first 100 days of the hold period.

By implementing rigorous, activity-based costing models, we accurately burden each product with its true operational cost—including changeover time and specific overhead. This exposes the SKUs that are secretly margin-dilutive. Armed with this data, we either mandate significant, immediate price increases on these complex items to justify their production, or we discontinue them entirely. Often, eliminating the bottom 20% of SKUs results in a negligible drop in top-line revenue but a massive surge in EBITDA.

This 'simplification' strategy is transformative. It frees up critical line time for the production of high-margin, high-volume core products, dramatically reduces working capital requirements, and drastically simplifies the procurement and forecasting process. A streamlined, highly efficient product portfolio signals to potential buyers at exit that the facility is a highly optimized, cash-generating machine rather than a chaotic, reactive job shop.
